items.title: 5. Methane Emission by Decaying Organic Matter

source_refs.note: 5. Methane Emission by Decaying Organic Matter: a main subheading of 33.5 Effect of Water Pollution on the Environment, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 255-256.

blocks.text: When sewage, agricultural runoff, or industrial waste enters water bodies, it boosts the growth of algae and other organisms. As these organisms die and decompose in oxygen-poor (anaerobic) conditions, methane, a potent greenhouse gas, is released. The excess methane contributes to climate change and worsens global warming.
a) Methylmercury ([CH₃Hg]⁺) is “highly fat-soluble,” allowing it to cross biological membranes and the blood-brain barrier.

blocks.prompt: (i) Contrast the chemical structure of the methylmercury cation ([CH₃Hg]⁺) with the inorganic mercury ion (Hg²⁺). Explain why the presence of the methyl group (-CH₃) alters its solubility in lipid bilayers of living cells compared to the inorganic ion.
blocks.explanation: Hg²⁺ is a small ion with a 2+ charge; water molecules surround it strongly, so it stays in water and cannot cross the non-polar lipid bilayer. In [CH₃Hg]⁺ a non-polar methyl group is bonded to mercury and the charge is only 1+, so it is less polar, dissolves in the lipid bilayer, and crosses cell membranes and the blood-brain barrier.

rows: A mercury ion only, no organic group
A non-polar –CH₃ group bonded to mercury
Strongly surrounded by water molecules (more polar)
Less polar, more soluble in fat
Crosses the lipid bilayer with difficulty
Crosses the lipid bilayer and the blood-brain barrier easily

blocks.prompt: (ii) Predict the impact on the “biomagnification” process if ([CH₃Hg]⁺) was highly water-soluble but had low fat solubility.
blocks.explanation: Biomagnification would be much less: a water-soluble substance is quickly removed from the body (in urine, for example) and is not stored in fatty tissues, so it would not build up at each step of the food chain.

blocks.prompt: b) How the water pollution can contribute to the global warming?
blocks.explanation: Water rich in sewage and nutrients boosts the growth of algae and other organisms; when these die and decompose under oxygen-poor (anaerobic) conditions, methane, a potent greenhouse gas, is released.
